correctness.rationale: Six-times tetrahedron volume is multiaffine in four vertices, enabling prism-vertex reduction and requiring all positive endpoint combinations at an equality point to remain extremal with common orientation. Every strict 3+1 vertex split is suboptimal against a crossed-chord 2+2 split; hence equal-height rigidity holds for all tetrahedra, including interior corners. For four cyclic polygon vertices, crossed determinant is 4R² times three sin(pi*(gi+gj)/n) factors. The symmetric strictly concave log product is maximized by balanced positive integer gaps, producing the known scalar value and N=n/2*binom(4,n mod 4) distinct lower/upper assignments. Edge-endpoint binary choices yield exact complete-face equality criterion and dimension 0/1/2 for residues 0,odd,2 mod4. Independently tested n=4..20 crossed-chord maxima/optimal counts and n=4..15 endpoint-cell dimension. Numerical volume formula is prior, not claimed new.
